title: [Back Order] LG 29 Inch 2560x1080 IPS 100Hz Ultrawide 21:9 Monitor $239 Delivered @ LG  (Also a 27" for $159)
body:
Deal: [Back Order] LG 29 Inch 2560x1080 IPS 100Hz Ultrawide 21:9 Monitor $239 Delivered @ LG  (Also a 27" for $159)

[aiyoyo] This monitor USB Type-C just for display and data not for charging laptop as far as I can see, am I right?
[DisasterArea] Will tell you when it arrives…. but I think you're correct, I believe LG use an external power brick so USB-C power is unlikely.
Power is not mentioned but it deos say "This monitor offers USB Type-C™, DisplayPort, HDMI ports to ensure smooth connectivity with various devices. The USB Type-C™ port supports both display output and data transfer, allowing easy connection to your laptop with a single cable."
[notaccel] yeah, just display and data from this USB C port, AC adapter is only rated for 19v 1.7a.
[goig986] @iSmart: the PPI on LG 29 Inch 2560x1080 is lower than a 27" 2K screen. So it's worse.
[Sunnyoz] For another $60 this ones seems to be good deal for a 34”
https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/965367
[DisasterArea] If you're having one single screen dead ahead of you, I'd definitely look at that Philips, unless you're using a console, then a normal 16:9 is better IMHO>
Nothing wrong with fastVA panels.
As I'm putting mine above another screen I didn't want a lot of vertical height, but wanted it to match my 32" screen width and as close as possible dot pitch resolution.
It's a bonus it does both these things, and is 21:9 (movie resolution)..
So this one is perfect for "two extra computers" screens (or side by side windows) as well as "movies". works well.
I use my screens for multi-pc lab use and work, and xbox… so have come to the conclusion that the dot pitch of a 1080P 24", a 1440P 32" and this 21:9 2560x1080 all match. I've had super ultrawide and 4K etc, just dont hit the spot for me.
[Big L] The reviews are concerning regarding reliability
[wayl] I need a cheap but good OLED instead! AW2726DM jumped up in price to $699!
[Consumer123] Any good for productivity and text heavy work?
